text:
micah: Heads up — seeing sharp e2w p95 spikes across a subset of GPU racks during the 11:30-12:00 batchwave. Latency goes from ~3ms to 40-120ms for short windows (~30-90s). Not all racks, looks like a rack group in us-west-2a.
sarah_ops: Saw the traces too. Packet loss counters tick during the spike, and RDMA retransmits increase.
jonathan: Any recent MTU/tor changes?
micah: Not in deploy log for that region. No config pushes in the last 24h.
kelsey: Quick paste from the node with the worst numbers: ```ethtool -k mlx5_core``` shows LRO on for some interfaces (we expect off). Also `/proc/net/softnet_stat` shows a backlog spike.
micah: hmm LRO should be disabled on our RDMA NICs. Could be config drift after kernel bump. Which kernel on that host?
sarah_ops: Kernel 5.15.42 -> kernel team did a rolling bump yesterday morning on a small subset. Might coincide.
infra-oncall: deploy-bot reports a canary kernel rollout at 08:15 UTC affecting rack-group rg-west-3.
jonathan: If LRO/SG offload re-enabled it can coalesce and break our RDMA path MTU assumptions, causing larger packets to fragment and amplify p95 under batching.
kelsey: quick check command to confirm MTU/frag: ```ip -s link show dev eth0``` and `rdma res show` on the host. I dumped ifconfig and saw MTU 9216 on one host and 1500 on another in same rack. That's bad.
micah: whoa mixed MTUs between nodes in same rack? That explains reassembly/fragment churn. Any chance of jumbo-negotiation failures on TOR?
sarah_ops: TOR logs show LLDP/MTU negotiation flapping for the pair of leaf switches returned by the switch mgmt: stash of events around 11:25. Suspect neighbor mismatch after the kernel bump changed NIC offload defaults.
jonathan: Proposed immediate mitigation: pin batch traffic for affected customer pools to non-affected racks (route by policy) and disable batching burst for 30m to avoid hitting the bad path. Also push a temporary tc qdisc change to limit TX burst.
micah: Agree. Can we do a quick BGP or ECMP reweight to shift traffic?
kelsey: I can inject a traffic-engineering rule for the affected racks to drop them from the preferred path for the next 45m. Will open a change and post the ID.
infra-oncall: change id: CHG-3487 opened to shift routing and apply tc burst-limit. ETA 5m.
sarah_ops: For root cause, plan: correlate kernel rollout hosts -> check NIC driver configs -> audit ansible role that manages ethtool settings -> run tor firmware/mtu audit.
jonathan: Also revalidate RDMA path MTU discovery; add a quick probe job to measure path MTU across all gpu nodes every 5m for 2h. If anything <9000 mark as degraded.
micah: Can we get a quick script to run probes and upload to S3 + alert if >5% of the pairs are degraded?
kelsey: writing probe now: uses `tracepath` + `ibv_devinfo` and outputs csv. Will run ad-hoc then schedule.
micah: Thanks. For the short term: 1) routing change in flight 2) limit batching burst 3) rollback kernel on a single canary rack if issue persists 4) full rollback plan if rollback fixes.
sarah_ops: Noted. I'll follow up with kernel team and tor team. If they confirm driver default changes, we need an automated guard in ansible to enforce offload flags.
jonathan: After we stabilise, add an e2e regression test for MTU-tolerant batching: simulate mismatched MTU and ensure batch windows don't cascade p95.
micah: Good call. Also add a metric: rdma_retransmits_per_min and net_frag_errors to the batch-window dashboard.
infra-oncall: CHG-3487 completed: routing change applied, tc burst-limit active. Early signs: p95 dropped from 120ms to ~6-10ms. Monitoring for 30m. :thumbsup:
kelsey: probe run results (t0): 58 of 324 pairs show MTU < 9000, mostly in rg-west-3. uploading csv: https://s3.redwood-internal/probes/1729997777-mtu-probe.csv
sarah_ops: Kernel team admits the kernel module update toggled `gro`/`lro` defaults for mlx5. They have a revert candidate.
micah: If revert candidate looks safe, roll it to the rest of the canary set after we stabilise routing.
jonathan: Postmortem TODOs already: add automated ansible check, probe job, dashboard metrics, and a runbook entry: "MTU/Offload-induced RDMA spikes during batching".
micah: Thanks all. Keep thread updated if any regression. If p95 climbs again revert the kernel immediately and escalate to infra-ops.
sarah_ops: will do. Monitoring alert set: e2w_batch_p95_spike -> page on >3x baseline for 2 consecutive windows.
micah: closing the loop: current status 15m after mitigation: stable. Leaving the routing change in place until full driver fix or ansible guard deployed. :lock:
kelsey: FYI we found two nodes with mismatched firmware on NICs; opening firmware CHG-3491 to align.
infra-oncall: CHG-3491 opened.
micah: Solid. Thanks team.
